claims.statement: NestedSpawnService is the gated entrypoint for nested multi-agent spawning: an operator-armed root is created via createRoot, and the root or any depth-permitted descendant spawns sub-agents via requestSpawn, called same-process (internal) or over HTTP by a runtime child shelling out with its scoped token.

Actual worktree and lease materialization is delegated to LoopService.prepareNestedLease, which reuses createWorktree/writeWorkAssignment/writeAssignmentPacket/insertWorkerLease unchanged, so a nested child is a real worker_leases row carrying parent_lease_id/spawn_tree_id/depth lineage rather than a parallel structure.

The spawn-tree id is the root lease id (spawn_trees.id == root worker_leases.id), so the root's own spawn token scoped to (rootLeaseId, treeId) validates when the root later calls requestSpawn with requested_by_lease_id = rootLeaseId.

The sub_agent_spawns table is a durable audit and budget ledger whose prompt_digest (sha256 of role|prompt|capability_ids) and parent/child/requester lineage make the cycle guard durable, and whose status CHECK includes requested/gated_out/prepared/running/completed/failed/cancelled with child_lease_id nullable because a gated_out spawn created no child.
The depth budget is default-deny: SPAWN_DEPTH_BUDGET env defaults to 0 (off), mirroring RUNTIME_ALLOW_SKIP_PERMISSIONS, so depth > tree.depth_budget gates out with depth_budget_exceeded.

requestSpawn applies an ordered gate chain — token/scope, operator pause, depth budget, cycle guard, cumulative token/wall budget, capability routing, then concurrency cap — and the first failure short-circuits into gateOut, writing an audited gated_out row with a reject_reason and emitting SWARM_SPAWN_GATED_OUT without materializing a lease.

The cumulative per-tree token/wall budgets are the hard bound while the per-depth grant is a configurable ceiling (SPAWN_PER_DEPTH_TOKEN_CAP default 50000, SPAWN_PER_DEPTH_WALL_CAP_MS default 120000) rather than total/(depth_budget+1), so one child cannot grab the whole tree.

Capability routing requires each bound capability to exist, be live (not disabled/deprecated and live_route_allowed), not list the ${role}:${runtime} action in forbidden_actions, and have a risk_ceiling at or above the tree risk_class.
The per-tree concurrency cap counts only real in-flight child spawns (depth > 0 in prepared/running status) and excludes the depth-0 root so max_concurrent_children=1 does not block the first child.
A child may spawn its own children only while above the depth floor (allowNestedSpawn = depth < depth_budget), and only then is a real child-scoped spawn token minted and returned to the caller.

An operator pause is a soft denial for nested spawns: assertOperatorNotPaused mapping LOOP_OPERATOR_PAUSED produces a gated_out row with reason operator_paused and no lease, worktree, or budget mutation.

Spawn tokens are HMAC-scoped credentials of shape base64url("leaseId|spawnTreeId|expiresAt").sig with a 30-minute TTL; validation is constant-time on the signature and never throws, returning false for malformed/expired/wrong-scope tokens which surfaces as SPAWN_TOKEN_INVALID (HTTP 401).

The spawn-token secret resolves through DJIMITFLO_SPAWN_TOKEN_SECRET then JWT_SECRET, fails closed with SPAWN_TOKEN_SECRET_REQUIRED in production when neither is set, and uses a per-process ephemeral secret in local/test.

Token flow is asymmetric to break a LoopService→NestedSpawnService cycle: token logic lives in the leaf module spawn-token.ts, LoopService only mints (buildNestedSpawnEnv injects DJIMITFLO_SPAWN_TOKEN/DJIMITFLO_CONTROL_URL/DJIMITFLO_LEASE_ID/DJIMITFLO_SPAWN_TREE_ID for an armed lease), and NestedSpawnService only validates at requestSpawn.

The raw spawn token is never persisted or written into the assignment file: the Nested Spawn Control block rendered in the assignment shows <redacted> and instructs the runtime to read the token from its env.

spawn_trees gains optional additive context_budget/context_consumed columns (SPAWN_CONTEXT_BUDGET default 0 = no isolation); createRoot detects them via PRAGMA table_info and includes them only when present to keep the insert backward-compatible.

The /api/swarms/spawns router mounts BEFORE the generic /swarms requireAuth mount in the route table so the specific path wins, and both are guarded by requireAuthOrSpawnToken which admits EITHER a Bearer JWT (setting req.user) OR an X-Spawn-Token header (leaving req.user unset).

A malformed/expired Bearer token returns 401 AUTH_INVALID and never falls through to the spawn-token path, while an X-Spawn-Token header passes through with real scope/expiry validation deferred to requestSpawn downstream.

Because POST /spawns/root sits behind requirePermission('write:swarm_action') which 401s when req.user is unset, a token-only runtime child can POST /spawns but can never create roots — only operators arm trees.
The HTTP spawn route never trusts a request-body internal flag; it always calls requestSpawn with internal:false so same-process orchestrators using internal:true cannot be impersonated over HTTP.

Spawn outcomes are observable end-to-end: SWARM_SPAWN_PREPARED and SWARM_SPAWN_GATED_OUT events broadcast the spawn id, tree, lineage, depth, runtime, role, status, and reject reason, and getSpawnStatus/listSpawnTree read back from sub_agent_spawns.

The control URL is derived at server startup (127.0.0.1 when binding 0.0.0.0/localhost) so a same-host runtime child can call back without operator config, and operators override DJIMITFLO_CONTROL_URL for Docker or remote children.

buildNestedSpawnEnv returns the MERGED runtime env (PATH/HOME/model keys) plus the DJIMITFLO_* control channel because executeRuntimeCommand replaces rather than merges env, and returns undefined for non-armed leases so ordinary loops fall back to buildRuntimeEnv unchanged.

No-theater caveat: the service makes spawning and audit real, but whether the child process actually runs and self-spawns depends on the runtime — mock echoes with no self-spawn while codex/claude shell out to the control endpoint, and the gates are exercised identically either way.

The nested-spawn page's related pages retarget the security-model concept to AuthN/AuthZ: Roles, JWT Sessions & WebSocket Auth (concepts/roles-and-permissions.md), which documents the requireAuth/requirePermission middleware and RBAC default-deny posture that nested spawning mirrors.

The nested-spawn page's related pages retarget the swarm control-plane concept to the Maker–Checker Loop Execution workflow (workflows/maker-checker-loop.md), which documents the goal/daemon queue under which the /api/swarms/spawns control routes are mounted.
